entries.title: Observation-equivalence boundary for simple versus complex contagion
entries.locator: Section6.1 final paragraph; printed page25; zero-based PDF page24; lines976-979
entries.posed_question: Distinguish simple from complex contagion from empirical observations.
entries.status_reason: 2026 roadmap poses the challenge but published and preprint classifiers already address important instances; exact narrowed identification boundary has not been certified novel or currently open.

closest_prior.citation: Cencetti et al. Phys Rev Lett130,247401(2023)

closest_prior.citation: Contreras et al. PLOS Computational Biology20,e1012206(2024)
closest_prior.access: roadmap reference245 and SH2025 related-work discussion read; original not independently read

closest_prior.established_baseline: Classification and parameter regression from topological summaries of simulated contagion on empirical network structures; includes partial observability experiments.

entries.our_target: For a specified finite known-graph family, seed regime, observation channel and parameter ranges, characterize when independent-edge infection and a reinforced-threshold law produce overlapping observed infection-time distributions; state what additional observation or controlled exposure separates them.
assumptions: Homophily either represented or explicitly excluded
Parameter ranges and seed regime fixed
entries.significance: Clarify which data support mechanism identification and when classification cannot resolve the competing mechanisms.
entries.interface: individual adoption -> interaction groups -> partial histories -> mechanism-compatible set -> intervention decision
entries.existing_corpus_match: None established; generic connectivity and probe-injectivity statements do not supply the competing laws or discriminator.
entries.lowest_cost_discriminator: Compare exact observation laws on two-to-four-node graphs after reading the closest model definitions; seek a nontrivial collision or separation; reject routine existing characterization.
entries.novelty_requirement: A defensible class-wide identification or robustness boundary, not another classifier implementation.
entries.followup_before_execution: Compare source models and SH2025 limitations; review subsequent work on partial observation, censoring, homophily and exact law identification.

entries.title: Sharp jointly biased direct and spillover-effect regions
entries.locator: Section3.6.3 Other types of biases and Sharpness results; HTML lines522-526
entries.posed_question: Sensitivity to selection, missingness, measurement and interference, potentially jointly.
entries.status_reason: Source poses the general challenge; SM2020 already treats multiple biases. Exact added interference/measurement interaction and current novelty remain unverified.

closest_prior.established_baseline: Composite risk-ratio bias bounds combining confounding, selection and exposure/outcome misclassification; abstract-level comparison only.

closest_prior.access: CI2025 sharpness discussion names these established results; original theorems not independently reviewed

entries.our_target: Under a fixed network exposure map, characterize a sharp identified region for one specified direct or spillover contrast with jointly exposure-dependent outcome misclassification and sample selection; provide attaining compatible models and a nonroutine analytic or computational improvement over response-type enumeration.
assumptions: True versus recorded peer exposure distinguished
entries.significance: Avoid unsupported combination of independent corrections and give an exact causal-effect boundary under a defended joint model.
entries.interface: true individual/group outcomes -> selection/measurement operators -> observed sample -> causal-effect region
entries.existing_corpus_match: None; assumed additive numerical bias intervals do not derive this identified region or sharpness.
entries.lowest_cost_discriminator: Map one small cluster's variables and restrictions onto the existing multiple-bias framework before deriving bounds; test whether the proposed target collapses to a known result.
entries.novelty_requirement: Uncovered joint interference/bias case with exact gains; generic finite LP formulation or bias warning alone is insufficient.
entries.followup_before_execution: Read full SM2020 and network sensitivity papers; compare estimands, dependence assumptions, sharpness and subsequent 2026 results.

entries.title: Structural power and balanced bargaining ranking agreement
entries.locator: Section3.4 final paragraphs; author-preprint HTML lines375-378
entries.kind: explicit mathematical characterization, counterexample and complexity problem
entries.posed_question: When do structural power and balanced bargaining payoff rankings agree?
entries.status_reason: Recent author-posed question verified, but exact index version, graph class and closest theorem/subsequent-work comparison remain incomplete.

closest_prior.access: source discussion and reference139 read; guessed author PDF inaccessible; original full-theorem comparison outstanding

entries.our_target: Fix one source-exact index g and characterize a graph class with matching-conditioned, existential or robust ranking agreement; keep quantifiers distinct; find a smallest graph separating agreement notions and certify minimality within a declared bounded class.
entries.formal_statement_component: For nonempty balanced-outcome set B(G), robust agreement requires g_i>g_j to imply inf_{x in B(G)}(x_i-x_j)>0.
assumptions: Exchange rule, weights and outside options fixed
Union over all maximum-weight matchings distinguished from a fixed matching
No coordinatewise interval substitution for dependent payoff vectors
entries.significance: Determine when structural power predicts bargaining payoff orderings rather than merely correlating with them.
entries.interface: exchange graph -> structural index and bargaining mechanism -> payoff-outcome set -> observed ordering
entries.existing_corpus_match: None; two_person_budget_iff lacks exchange graphs, structural index, matchings and balanced outcomes.
entries.lowest_cost_discriminator: Recover exact index definitions and existing class results; compare one four-node experimental network and one graph with nonunique maximum matching.
entries.novelty_requirement: A source-matched agreement class, nontrivial separating counterexample or complexity result, not routine balanced-outcome computation.
entries.followup_before_execution: Original index and bargaining papers, source publication-version comparison and subsequent solutions.

Priors and evidence held fixed across comparisons
entries.significance: Identify which psychological/social ranking predictions survive probabilistic reformulation and propose distinguishing empirical contrasts.

entries.followup_before_execution: Find comparable Bayesian expectation-states reconstructions, exact path-index models and more recent ordinal-equivalence results.

entries.our_target: In a declared two-process marked birth/death model, derive necessary and sufficient measurement/exclusion restrictions for separately identifying recognition and congestion effects. Compare an observation-equivalent mechanism pair, then add a specified measure or defended variation and characterize the newly identified or sharply partially identified effect.
assumptions: Latent process and observation laws fixed
Common causes of recognition and congestion addressed
Regulatory changes need defended exclusions rather than assumed instrument status
entries.significance: Explain when equal counts and event histories support different mechanisms, and identify observations that would separate them.

entries.novelty_requirement: A source-relevant minimal observation design or sharp process-specific identified region beyond standard latent-state results.
entries.followup_before_execution: Compare organizational-form empirical measurement models, marked-process identification and subsequent work; define one exact target with defended assumptions.
